title: swallowing this pill for female health

segments.text: I swallowed this tiny machine that tells me what my core body temperature is. So, this is this like heavy metal pill, and you swallow it, and right now I have one inside of me. And then I have this monitor that connects [music] to it via Bluetooth or something wireless. And so, it transmits through my stomach [music] what my core body temperature is. Right now, my core body temperature is 36.96 [music] C, and I have 500 pieces of data, so 500 minutes of data to offload from the pill that's in my belly onto

this machine. Kind of crazy, but this is one of 50-ish devices that I'm using to measure my entire menstrual cycle. We're collecting something like 1,900 biomarkers. We're spending $2.5 million on this, and it will be the most quantified menstrual [music] cycle ever. We're trying to do something that no one's ever done before because the literature around female health is so sparse, but we're looking at things like [music] grip strength, my sleep, my HRV, my sense of smell, my sense of taste, [music] my brain age, my skin age, my gut microbiome, my vaginal microbiome.

We're measuring all these different things, and one of the more important things we're measuring is my body temperature cuz after ovulation, your body temperature rises by half a degree Fahrenheit. And a lot of women will use an under the tongue thermometer, which I use every morning, too, as well. But this is less accurate, we think, than the internal temperature. And so, we'll be able to see what the difference is between the two. If you're relying on under the tongue for ovulation so that you can track when to get pregnant, it might not be 100% accurate. So, we'll see. We'll report out. So, we'll also be able to see exactly how and how quickly my body temperature changes as I

ovulate. Pretty cool. I'm excited [music] to share the results. Everything we're doing, we're going to be posting online for free. So, if you're interested in following along, I'm on day 16 of this crazy [music] experiment, and yeah, it's been really tough, but I'm super excited to find out what we learn about female [music] health. So, follow along if you want to learn more.
